metadata.title: Boosting the Margin: A New Explanation for the Effectiveness of Voting Methods
metadata.authors: Robert E. Schapire, Yoav Freund, Peter Bartlett, Wee Sun Lee
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Convex hull of base classifiers
nodes.statement: Convex hull $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathcal{H}$: the set of mappings $f = \sum_{h} a_h h$ with $a_h \ge 0$, $\sum_h a_h = 1$, only finitely many $a_h$ nonzero.
nodes.statement_clean: The set of finitely-supported convex combinations of base classifiers in $\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.name: Classification margin (binary case)
nodes.statement: For an example $(x,y) \in X \times \{-1,+1\}$ and $f \in \mathcal{C}$, the margin is $y f(x)$. The combined classifier $\mathrm{sign}(f)$ misclassifies $(x,y)$ iff $y f(x) \le 0$; the margin lies in $[-1,1]$.
nodes.statement_clean: The (signed) confidence of the combined vote on a labeled example: positive for correct, negative for incorrect.

nodes.name: Margin distribution graph
nodes.statement: The cumulative distribution function $\theta \mapsto P_S[y f(x) \le \theta]$ over the training sample $S$, plotted for $\theta \in [-1,1]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Plot of the empirical CDF of margins over the training set.

nodes.name: VC-dimension
nodes.statement: For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $\{-1,+1\}$-valued functions on $X$, the VC-dimension is the largest $d$ such that there exist $x_1,\ldots,x_d \in X$ with $|\{(f(x_1),\ldots,f(x_d)) : f \in \mathcal{F}\}| = 2^d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Largest size of a sample shattered by the function class.

nodes.name: Approximating set $\mathcal{C}_N$
nodes.statement: For integer $N \ge 1$, $\mathcal{C}_N = \{ f = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N h_i : h_i \in \mathcal{H} \}$, the set of unweighted averages of $N$ elements of $\mathcal{H}$ (with repetition allowed).
nodes.statement_clean: Sloppy cover of $\mathcal{C}$ by $N$-element averages of base classifiers.

nodes.name: Sloppy cover
nodes.statement: For a class $\mathcal{F}$ of real-valued functions, sample size $m$, $\theta > 0$, $\epsilon > 0$: $\hat{\mathcal{F}}$ is an $\epsilon$-sloppy $\theta$-cover of $\mathcal{F}$ w.r.t. sample $S$ if for every $f \in \mathcal{F}$ there is $\hat f \in \hat{\mathcal{F}}$ with $P_{(x,y) \sim S}[|f(x)-\hat f(x)| > \theta] \le \epsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: An $\epsilon$-fraction-sloppy uniform $\theta$-approximation of $\mathcal{F}$ on the sample.

nodes.name: Multiclass margin
nodes.statement: For base classifiers $h: X \times Y \to \{0,1\}$ and $f \in \mathcal{C}$, the margin of $(x,y)$ is $\mathrm{margin}(x,y) = f(x,y) - \max_{\ell \ne y} f(x,\ell)$. The classifier predicts $\arg\max_\ell f(x,\ell)$ and is wrong iff $\mathrm{margin}(x,y) \le 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Difference between vote weight on the true label and the largest weight on any other label.

nodes.name: Bias and variance (Kong-Dietterich)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Bias} = \mathrm{err}(C^*) - \mathrm{err}(C_B)$, $\mathrm{Variance} = E_S[\mathrm{err}(C_S)] - \mathrm{err}(C^*)$, where $C_S$ is the classifier from sample $S$, $C^*$ the plurality-vote rule over infinitely many samples, and $C_B$ the Bayes optimal rule.
nodes.statement_clean: Persistent error of the aggregate rule (bias) plus excess error from sample fluctuations (variance).

nodes.name: Bias and variance (Breiman)
nodes.statement: Partition the sample space into the unbiased set $U = \{x : C^*(x) = C_B(x)\}$ and its complement (biased set). $\mathrm{Bias} = P[(x,y): \mathrm{biased}] \cdot E_S[\mathrm{err}(C_S \mid \mathrm{biased})]$ and similarly for $\mathrm{Variance}$ using $U$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bias/variance assigned by partitioning instance space according to whether the aggregate rule matches Bayes optimal.

nodes.name: Margin bound for finite base-classifier spaces
nodes.statement: For finite $\mathcal{H}$, sample $S$ of size $m$, with probability $\ge 1-\delta$ over $S$, every $f \in \mathcal{C}$ and every $\theta > 0$ satisfy $P_\mathcal{D}[y f(x) \le 0] \le P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] + O\!\left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left( \frac{\log m \, \log|\mathcal{H}|}{\theta^2} + \log(1/\delta) \right)^{1/2} \right)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generalization error of any majority vote is bounded by the empirical fraction with margin below $\theta$ plus a term that grows with $\log|\mathcal{H}|$ and shrinks in $1/\sqrt{m}$ and in $\theta$.
assumptions: Examples drawn i.i.d. from a distribution $\mathcal{D}$ over $X \times \{-1,+1\}$
conclusions: $P_\mathcal{D}[y f(x) \le 0] \le P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] + O\!\left( m^{-1/2} \sqrt{\theta^{-2} \log m \, \log|\mathcal{H}| + \log(1/\delta)} \right)$ uniformly in $f \in \mathcal{C}$ and $\theta > 0$
nodes.notes: Original PDF math is partly garbled; LaTeX reconstruction follows Bartlett 1998-style margin bound.

nodes.name: Margin bound for infinite base-classifier spaces (VC version)
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{H}$ has VC-dimension $d$ and $d \le m$, then with probability $\ge 1-\delta$, for every $f \in \mathcal{C}$ and every $\theta > 0$: $P_\mathcal{D}[y f(x) \le 0] \le P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] + O\!\left( m^{-1/2} \left( \frac{d \log^2(m/d)}{\theta^2} + \log(1/\delta) \right)^{1/2} \right)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Same as Theorem 1 but with $\log|\mathcal{H}|$ replaced by VC-dimension $d$ (with extra log factors).
conclusions: $P_\mathcal{D}[y f(x) \le 0] \le P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] + O\!\left( m^{-1/2} \sqrt{\theta^{-2} d \log^2(m/d) + \log(1/\delta)} \right)$

nodes.name: Devroye uniform-deviation bound
nodes.statement: For any class $\mathcal{A}$ of subsets of $X$ and i.i.d. sample of size $m$, $P_S[\sup_{A \in \mathcal{A}} | P_S[A] - P_\mathcal{D}[A] | > \epsilon] \le 4 \Pi_\mathcal{A}(2m) \exp(-m \epsilon^2 / 2)$, where $\Pi_\mathcal{A}(n) = \max_{|S|=n} |\{A \cap S : A \in \mathcal{A}\}|$ is the growth function.
nodes.statement_clean: Bounds the probability that empirical and true probabilities differ uniformly over a set system, sharper than Vapnik-Chervonenkis by a factor of 2 in the exponent.

nodes.name: Sloppy-cover generalization bound
nodes.statement: For a class $\mathcal{F}$ of real-valued functions and any $\theta > 0$, $\epsilon > 0$: the probability over $S$ that there exists $f \in \mathcal{F}$ with $P_\mathcal{D}[y f(x) \le 0] - P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] > \epsilon$ is at most $2 \, \mathcal{N}(\mathcal{F}, \theta/2, \epsilon/8, 2m) \, \exp(-\epsilon^2 m / 32)$, where $\mathcal{N}$ is the size of the smallest $(\epsilon/8)$-sloppy $(\theta/2)$-cover.
nodes.statement_clean: General sloppy-cover-based generalization bound; specialized via probabilistic constructions to give Theorems 1 and 2.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F}$ is a class of real-valued functions on $X$

nodes.name: AdaBoost margin distribution bound
nodes.statement: If AdaBoost is run with base classifiers having weighted training errors $\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_T$, then for any $\theta$, $P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] \le 2^T \prod_{t=1}^T \sqrt{\epsilon_t^{1-\theta} (1-\epsilon_t)^{1+\theta}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fraction of training examples with margin below $\theta$ decays as a product over rounds; if every $\epsilon_t \le 1/2 - \gamma$ and $\theta < \gamma$, the bound is exponentially small in $T$.
assumptions: AdaBoost is run for $T$ rounds with base learner producing $h_t$ at weighted error $\epsilon_t$

nodes.name: Multiclass margin generalization bound
nodes.statement: For finite $\mathcal{H}$ over $X \times Y$ (and analogously for VC-dimension $d$), with probability $\ge 1-\delta$, every $f \in \mathcal{C}$ and every $\theta > 0$ satisfy $P_\mathcal{D}[\mathrm{margin}_f(x,y) \le 0] \le P_S[\mathrm{margin}_f(x,y) \le \theta] + O\!\left( m^{-1/2} \sqrt{ \theta^{-2} \log m \, \log|\mathcal{H}| + \log(1/\delta) } \right)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multiclass extension of Theorems 1 and 2: replaces $y f(x)$ by the multiclass margin.
assumptions: $\mathcal{H}$ is finite (or has VC-dimension $d$ in the second part)
conclusions: $P_\mathcal{D}[\mathrm{margin}_f \le 0] \le P_S[\mathrm{margin}_f \le \theta] + O(\cdot)$ (same form as TP115.1 / TP115.2)

nodes.name: AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Iteratively reweights training examples and combines weak base classifiers into a weighted majority vote.
nodes.pseudocode: Initialize $D_1(i) = 1/m$. For $t = 1,\ldots,T$: train base learner with distribution $D_t$ to obtain $h_t$ with weighted error $\epsilon_t = P_{i \sim D_t}[h_t(x_i) \ne y_i]$; set $\alpha_t = \tfrac{1}{2} \ln((1-\epsilon_t)/\epsilon_t)$; update $D_{t+1}(i) \propto D_t(i) \exp(-\alpha_t y_i h_t(x_i))$; output $H(x) = \mathrm{sign}(\sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x))$.

nodes.name: Bagging
nodes.statement: Trains the base learner on bootstrap subsamples of $S$ and combines the resulting classifiers by uniform voting.
nodes.pseudocode: For $t = 1,\ldots,T$: draw bootstrap sample $S_t$ from $S$ with replacement, train base learner on $S_t$ to obtain $h_t$. Output unweighted majority vote of $h_1,\ldots,h_T$.

nodes.name: Error-correcting output codes (ECOC) voting variant
nodes.statement: Reduces multiclass classification to many two-class problems by relabeling with random binary codes; combines predictions by Hamming-closest codeword (interpreted as voting).
nodes.pseudocode: For $t = 1,\ldots,T$: pick a random map $\pi_t : \{1,\ldots,K\} \to \{-1,+1\}$, relabel $S$ by $y' = \pi_t(y)$, train base learner on relabeled data to obtain $h_t$. Classify a test $x$ by the label whose codeword $(\pi_1(\ell),\ldots,\pi_T(\ell))$ is closest in Hamming distance to $(h_1(x),\ldots,h_T(x))$, equivalently the label receiving the most bit-votes.

nodes.name: Maximal-margin (optimal-margin) classification
nodes.statement: Given mapping $\phi: X \to \mathbb{R}^N$ and labeled sample $\{(x_i,y_i)\}$ with $y_i \in \{-1,+1\}$, find the unit vector $w \in \mathbb{R}^N$ maximizing $\min_i \frac{y_i \, w \cdot \phi(x_i)}{\|w\|_2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximum-margin linear separator in feature space (the SVM optimization).
nodes.origin_citation: Vapnik 1995; Boser, Guyon, Vapnik 1992; Cortes & Vapnik 1995

nodes.name: Tighter margin-based generalization bounds
nodes.statement: Find substantially tighter upper bounds on the generalization error of voting classifiers as a function of the empirical margin distribution (and possibly other statistics) than those given by Theorems 1 and 2.

nodes.name: Conditions for slow growth of weighted training errors in AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Characterize conditions under which the weighted training errors $\epsilon_t$ produced by AdaBoost stay bounded away from $1/2$ slowly enough for the bound of Theorem 5 to remain useful.

nodes.name: Support-vector-style bounds for boosting
nodes.statement: Investigate the relevance of Vapnik's support-vector-count generalization bounds for boosting in real-world problems.

nodes.name: Letter, satimage, vehicle benchmark experiments
nodes.statement: Empirical comparison of bagging, boosting and ECOC (using C4.5 and decision stumps as base learners) on the UCI letter, satimage and vehicle datasets, with learning curves and margin distribution graphs (Figures 1, 4, 5).

nodes.name: Coordinate-noise distribution where bagging fails
nodes.statement: Label $y \in \{-1,+1\}$ uniform; instance $x \in \{-1,+1\}^7$ with each coordinate equal to $y$ with prob.\ $0.9$. Base learner picks the single coordinate with smallest training error. Bayes error $\approx 0.3\%$, variance dominates, but bagging only reaches $5.6\%$ (and boosting reaches $0.6\%$).

nodes.name: Delta-function over-fitting example
nodes.statement: Base class $\mathcal{H}$ is delta functions plus the two constant functions. For any sample of size $m$, an unweighted majority over $\le 2m$ such functions perfectly fits the training data while having very poor generalization; AdaBoost-style voting drives training error to zero with margin $\Theta(1/m)$.

nodes.name: Bias-variance experiments on synthetic datasets
nodes.statement: Boosting and bagging on waveform, twonorm, threenorm, ringnorm and the Kong-Dietterich 2D 6-class problem, with bias and variance estimated under both Kong-Dietterich and Breiman definitions (Table 1). Boosting reduces error on ringnorm from $40.6\%$ to $12.2\%$ while *increasing* the variance.

nodes.name: Bound is loose for moderate $m$
nodes.statement: The asymptotic form of Theorem 1 is $P_\mathcal{D}[y f(x) \le 0] \le P_S[y f(x) \le \theta] + O\!\left( \sqrt{\log(1/\delta) / m + (\log m \, \log|\mathcal{H}|) / (m \theta^2)} \right)$; numerically meaningful only for $m$ in the tens of thousands.

nodes.name: Maximizing minimal margin can hurt
nodes.statement: Empirically (Breiman; Grove and Schuurmans), modifying AdaBoost to maximize the minimal margin (via linear programming) often *increases* generalization error, indicating the bound's predictive criterion is incomplete.

nodes.name: Connection between AdaBoost and maximal-margin classifiers
nodes.statement: Both AdaBoost and SVMs find a linear combination in a high-dimensional space with large margin; AdaBoost normalizes by $\|\alpha\|_1$ with $\|h(x)\|_\infty \le 1$, while SVMs normalize by $\|w\|_2$ in a Euclidean feature space.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Probabilistic construction of an $N$-element sloppy cover $\mathcal{C}_N$ of $\mathcal{C}$, decompose $P_\mathcal{D}[yf \le 0]$ via $\mathcal{C}_N$, apply Chernoff and union bounds, then optimize $N \sim \theta^{-2} \ln(m|\mathcal{H}|/\delta)$.

nodes.name: Build the approximating set $\mathcal{C}_N$
nodes.statement: Define $\mathcal{C}_N = \{ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N h_i : h_i \in \mathcal{H}\}$ and associate each $f = \sum_h a_h h \in \mathcal{C}$ with the distribution $Q_f$ on $\mathcal{H}$ given by the coefficients $a_h$; sampling $h_1,\ldots,h_N \sim Q_f$ yields a random $g \in \mathcal{C}_N$.

nodes.name: Two-term decomposition
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{C}$ and $\theta > 0$: $P_\mathcal{D}[yf \le 0] \le E_{g \sim Q_f} P_\mathcal{D}[yg \le \theta/2] + E_\mathcal{D} P_{g \sim Q_f}[yg \le \theta/2 \mid yf \le 0]$.

nodes.name: Bound the second term by Chernoff
nodes.statement: For fixed $(x,y)$, $y g(x)$ is the average of $N$ i.i.d.\ samples with mean $y f(x) \le 0$, so $P_{g \sim Q_f}[yg(x) > \theta/2] \le e^{-N \theta^2 / 8}$.

nodes.name: Union bound over $\mathcal{C}_N$
nodes.statement: There are $\le (m+1) |\mathcal{H}|^N$ relevant $(g,\theta)$ pairs; choosing $\delta_N = \delta/(N(N+1))$ and a Chernoff tail $e^{-m \epsilon_N^2 / 2}$ over $g \in \mathcal{C}_N$ gives that $P_\mathcal{D}[yg \le \theta/2] \le P_S[yg \le \theta/2] + \epsilon_N$ uniformly with prob.\ $\ge 1-\delta_N$.

nodes.name: Translate empirical $\theta/2$-margin back to $\theta$-margin of $f$
nodes.statement: Apply the same Chernoff argument inside $P_S$ to bound $P_S[yg \le \theta/2]$ by $P_S[yf \le \theta] + e^{-N \theta^2 / 8}$.

nodes.name: Optimize $N$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Combine the four bounds and set $N = \lceil 4 \theta^{-2} \ln(2m/\ln|\mathcal{H}|) \rceil$ (the precise choice that balances the exponential terms against the union bound) to obtain the stated bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Same structure as PP115.1 but replace the union bound over $\mathcal{C}_N$ with Devroye's lemma (Lemma 3) and Sauer's lemma to control the growth function of the relevant set system.

nodes.name: Define set system $\mathcal{A}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{A} = \{\{(x,y) : yg(x) \le \theta/2\} : g \in \mathcal{C}_N, \theta > 0\}$.

nodes.name: Bound growth function via Sauer
nodes.statement: Sauer's lemma gives $|\mathcal{H} \cap S^{(2m)}| \le (2em/d)^d$, hence the growth function $\Pi_\mathcal{A}(2m) \le ((2m+1)(2em/d)^d)^N$.

nodes.name: Apply Devroye's lemma
nodes.statement: Plug $\Pi_\mathcal{A}(2m)$ into Lemma 3 to obtain the uniform deviation bound; setting $\epsilon_N = \sqrt{(2/m) \ln(\Pi_\mathcal{A}(2m)/\delta_N)}$ controls the first term of (3).

nodes.name: Optimize $N$
nodes.statement: Setting $N = \lceil 4 \theta^{-2} \ln(m/d) \rceil$ balances the terms and yields the VC-dimension-based bound of Theorem 2.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: Replace the indicator $\mathbf{1}[yf(x) \le \theta]$ by the exponential $\exp(-y \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x) + \theta \sum_t \alpha_t)$, then exploit the recursion $D_{t+1}(i) \propto D_t(i) e^{-\alpha_t y_i h_t(x_i)}$ to telescope into $\prod_t Z_t$ where $Z_t = 2 \sqrt{\epsilon_t (1-\epsilon_t)}$.

nodes.name: Exponential upper bound on indicator
nodes.statement: If $y f(x) \le \theta$ then $\exp(-y \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x) + \theta \sum_t \alpha_t) \ge 1$; therefore $P_S[yf \le \theta] \le E_{i \sim S} \exp(-y_i \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x_i) + \theta \sum_t \alpha_t)$.

nodes.name: Telescope via $D_t$ recursion
nodes.statement: Use $D_{T+1}(i) = (1/m) \exp(-y_i \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x_i)) / \prod_t Z_t$ and $\sum_i D_{T+1}(i) = 1$ to get $E_{i \sim S} \exp(-y_i \sum_t \alpha_t h_t(x_i)) = \prod_t Z_t$.

nodes.name: Plug in $\alpha_t = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln((1-\epsilon_t)/\epsilon_t)$
nodes.statement: Then $Z_t = 2\sqrt{\epsilon_t(1-\epsilon_t)}$ and $e^{\theta \alpha_t} = ((1-\epsilon_t)/\epsilon_t)^{\theta/2}$, giving the product $\prod_t 2 \sqrt{\epsilon_t^{1-\theta}(1-\epsilon_t)^{1+\theta}}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Combining the previous steps yields $P_S[yf \le \theta] \le 2^T \prod_{t=1}^T \sqrt{\epsilon_t^{1-\theta}(1-\epsilon_t)^{1+\theta}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: Mirror the proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 with the multiclass margin: define $\mathcal{C}_N$ on $\mathcal{H}$, decompose with respect to a label $\ell^*$ achieving the max in (13), apply Chernoff and (Sauer + Devroye) for the finite and VC-dimension cases respectively.

nodes.name: AdaBoost weight update
nodes.statement: $D_{t+1}(i) = D_t(i) \, \exp(-\alpha_t y_i h_t(x_i)) / Z_t$, with $\alpha_t = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln((1-\epsilon_t)/\epsilon_t)$ and $Z_t = 2 \sqrt{\epsilon_t (1-\epsilon_t)}$.

nodes.name: AdaBoost combined classifier
nodes.statement: $f(x) = \sum_{t=1}^T \alpha_t h_t(x) / \sum_{t=1}^T \alpha_t$; final classifier is $\mathrm{sign}(f(x))$, and $y f(x)$ is the margin.
